shadow:
Some tiredness lives below sleep and cannot be reached by it. You wake, you do the list, you tick the things off, and underneath it all the body is heavy in a way that has nothing to do with how much you slept. The day asks for small efforts and the small efforts feel like lifting something far larger than they are.

This is inertia, and the mistake almost everyone makes is to read it as laziness or a failing of will. Look closer at the day and you will often find the stepping stones laid out in a circle. You are walking, the legs are moving, the chores get done, and the path quietly returns you to where you started.

The loop runs on small things. A detail, then another detail, none of them pointed anywhere, each one asking for a little life force and giving none back.

The way out is hidden in the size of the problem. Inertia tells you the change has to be huge to matter, and that is the lie that keeps the circle closed. One small step, off the loop, in a direction that is actually yours, is enough to break it. Small is the door.
repressive: Some people meet the heaviness by quietly agreeing with it. They can see the way out, they could describe it, and still they do not move. The will goes cold. They call the loop their nature and stop arguing with it.
reactive: Others meet it by never sitting still. They chase stimulation, switch tasks, fill every gap with motion so the flatness underneath stays drowned out. It looks like energy. No commitment ever holds long enough to lead anywhere.
gift:
The first step gets taken before readiness arrives, or it does not get taken at all. Not the leap, not the plan for the whole mountain. One step, the dull and ordinary kind, aimed at something that genuinely belongs to them.

That is where determination starts, and it is gentler than the word sounds. Most people hear determination and picture gritted teeth, a long fight against themselves. It is not that. It is the quiet discovery that the first step is the only one that costs real courage, and every step after it costs a little less.

What builds is a groove. Do the small thing again, and again, in the same true direction, and the path starts to hold its own shape. The energy that used to drain into the circle now runs forward. You can feel it. The doing gets lighter exactly as you would expect it to get harder.

And the mind, which spent the Shadow years narrating the mountain and the odds, begins to quiet. It has less to undermine. The further along the groove a person travels, the more it feels less like pushing and more like being carried. Something larger leans in behind the work.
siddhi:
Past a certain point the small stops being something a person manages and becomes the place the whole thing is hidden. Split a thread of energy in half, then half again, and you could go on forever. The infinitely small turns out to have no floor. It opens into the infinitely large.

Invincibility wears a hard name and means something soft. It is not armour. It is what is left when a person stops defending a separate self and lets their awareness dissolve back into the awareness of everything. Nothing can be taken from someone who is no longer holding a thing apart to keep. Nothing can be struck that has no edge.

This is the strength the Tao always pointed at, the kind that lives in water and in yielding, in a child running into the mist because the mist is beautiful. The whole universe folded into a hazelnut, and the hazelnut is love.

From here the long heavy years look different. The inertia was not a fault in you. It was the still ground the first real step had to be taken from.
